apiDocs.note: no OpenAPI document in the repo; the REST surface is declared by PHP controllers (Tier B)

notes: Routes are generic patterns, not a route table. client/src/router.js:104 declares ':controller', ':controller/create', ':controller/view/:id' and so on; the concrete screen list is those patterns expanded over the entity scopes in application/Espo/Resources/metadata/scopes/*.json where entity and object are both true (14 entities).

No route names a view component. A route resolves to a controller which picks its view at runtime from clientDefs metadata, so every route's component is null by design. Elements for these screens can only come from the crawl.
'*actions' (router.js:148) is the fallback handler, not a screen, and is skipped.

regions.name: RecordTable
regions.note: Every row carries data-id (the record id) and every cell data-name (the field). A row is addressable by the text of its key cell without any nth.

labelAssociation.note: No <label for>. Label and field are siblings inside .cell, and BOTH carry data-name with the model's field name. That attribute is the stronger handle: it is the app's own identifier, unaffected by translation, where the visible label is the translated string. Prefer data-name; fall back to the label-anchored template when a field name is unknown.

notes: data-action attributes (215 files) mark every clickable behaviour in the markup. They are the app's own action vocabulary and make excellent scoping selectors inside a component class.

auth.scheme: Espo auth token over HTTP Basic, or the Authorization-Token-Secret cookie in a browser session

users.note: the public demo gates on a user picker rather than a password — see app-profile.yaml

auth.note: GET /App/user with Basic credentials both authenticates and returns the token to reuse. This is the cheapest possible session: one request, no form, no CSRF.

authVerification.reason: /api/v1/Metadata answers 401 anonymously and 200 with the credential

endpoints.summary: create a record — the precondition workhorse
delete a record — use for test cleanup
the full metadata tree — field definitions for every entity, i.e. what a create payload may contain

notes: The API is generic: one set of CRUD routes serves every entity, with {entityType} taken from the 14 object scopes listed in routes.json. So a precondition for any entity is the same request with a different path segment — which is why this file lists the shapes rather than 14 copies of each.
The payload a create accepts is per entity and is declared in application/Espo/Resources/metadata/entityDefs/<entityType>.json. GET /api/v1/Metadata returns the same thing at runtime.
115 routes are declared in application/Espo/Resources/routes.json. The ones omitted here are admin, mail and stream operations no UI precondition needs; add a row when one does.
This is a PUBLIC DEMO. It resets periodically and may rate-limit. Treat write endpoints as usable but not guaranteed, and never assume data survives between runs.
